stories.title: A clean month in two warehouses
stories.recipe: Every bridge closes in quantity and value, and each account equals the GL.

stories.title: A transfer between warehouses on two accounts
stories.recipe: The transfer is a credit of 1310 and a debit of 1320, and no entity receipt.

stories.title: A transfer within one account
stories.recipe: Both sides of the transfer name 1311, so it is neither its debit nor its credit (I4).

stories.title: A transfer whose receiving side never arrived
stories.recipe: Riyadh closes on its own lines, but a transfer-out with no transfer-in is not proven.

stories.title: The receiving side posted in November
stories.recipe: The goods arrived on 31 October but were posted on 2 November: excluded, so the October transfer-out has no pair.

stories.title: A transfer received short and one at another value
stories.recipe: Two square metres short on one transfer, 75 riyals more on the other: each bridge closes on its own lines, but neither transfer is proven.

stories.title: A transfer in boxes received in pieces
stories.recipe: Twenty boxes left and 240 pieces arrived at the same value: no unit is converted (I1).

stories.title: One Transfer ID on two transfers
stories.recipe: Two transfers printed under one Transfer ID: which out went where is not proven.

stories.title: A negative closing the scope does not allow
stories.recipe: Fifty-five bags issued from forty: the closing is minus fifteen bags.

stories.title: The same register where negative balances are allowed
stories.recipe: The same bytes as M09; the confirmed scope allows negative balances (I6).

stories.title: A receipt written with a minus sign
stories.recipe: A return to the supplier written as a negative receipt: a movement carries no sign (I6).

stories.title: Boxes and pieces, and m3 and M3, in one position
stories.recipe: Units are compared as written: box and pcs, m3 and M3 (I1).

stories.title: A receipt posted in November
stories.recipe: Received on 30 October, posted on 1 November: not in this bridge, and the printed closing leaves it out (I2).

stories.title: September movements posted in October
stories.recipe: Posted in October, so in the bridge, and listed because they happened in September.

stories.title: The closing counts a receipt posted in November
stories.recipe: The stock system closed October with the November receipt in it.

stories.title: A return to the supplier of its receipt
stories.recipe: Twenty-five sheets of a 300-sheet receipt go back to the supplier.

stories.title: A return citing a receipt of another item
stories.recipe: Twenty bags of cement returned against a gypsum board receipt.

stories.title: A return citing an issue
stories.recipe: A return to the supplier must name a receipt, not an issue (I5).

stories.title: A customer return to another warehouse
stories.recipe: A customer brings back twelve pipes issued from Riyadh to Jeddah; the warehouse may differ (I5). The columns are printed in another order.

stories.title: Two returns beyond their receipt
stories.recipe: Sixty and fifty bags returned against a receipt of one hundred.

stories.title: A return of a September receipt
stories.recipe: The receipt returned is in September's register: listed, not held (I5).

stories.title: The same GL total with two accounts swapped
stories.recipe: The GL posted the cement receipt to the steel account: the totals agree, the accounts do not (I9).

stories.title: An account missing from the GL and one the register never names
stories.recipe: The GL file leaves out Jeddah and holds a goods-in-transit account no line names.

stories.title: A closing value one riyal off
stories.recipe: The quantities close; the printed closing value is 1.00 more than the bridge.

stories.title: A closing quantity one bag off
stories.recipe: The values close; the printed closing is one bag short.

stories.title: A new item without an opening and a position without its closing
stories.recipe: Sand was first received this month and has no opening line; cement in Riyadh has no closing line. Neither is taken as zero (I7).

stories.title: Two opening lines for one position
stories.recipe: One hundred and ninety-five pieces both printed as the opening.

stories.title: An opening dated in September
stories.recipe: The opening is dated 30 September, not 1 October.

stories.title: One Movement ID on two lines
stories.recipe: An issue in Riyadh and a receipt in Jeddah carry one Movement ID.

stories.title: One position on two accounts
stories.recipe: A Riyadh receipt posted to the Jeddah account: both accounts wait.

stories.title: An Item ID that reads as a formula
stories.recipe: An issue line whose item cannot be read could be any position's (I8).

stories.title: A write-down in Kuwaiti dinars
stories.recipe: A value adjustment of 125.500 dinars with a zero quantity, in three decimals.

stories.title: Yen with a fraction
stories.recipe: The yen has no decimals: 43000.5 does not read.

stories.title: A paged export repeating its headers
stories.recipe: Every page repeats the column row, in both files: listed and skipped (I10).

stories.title: One GL account on two lines
stories.recipe: The GL summary prints 1320 twice, once with zeros.

stories.title: A GL file that does not parse
stories.recipe: An unclosed quote in the GL summary: every account waits, the bridges do not (I10).

stories.title: A register not in UTF-8
stories.recipe: Saved as Windows Arabic: refused, nothing judged.

stories.title: A register without its Unit column
stories.recipe: Eleven columns: the register is not the contract's.

stories.title: A period that ends before it starts
stories.recipe: The confirmed period runs backwards: refused, nothing judged.

stories.title: Arabic dimensions and Arabic-Indic digits
stories.recipe: Arabic-Indic digits and the Arabic decimal separator read as Latin.

stories.title: Sixty positions across four accounts
stories.recipe: Volume within the structure: one closing a halala off holds its account only.

stories.title: Kinds the contract does not know
stories.recipe: Receipt with a capital letter and transfer without a direction.

stories.title: Links on the wrong lines
stories.recipe: A purchase order in the Origin ID of a receipt; a transfer-out without its Transfer ID.

stories.title: A position with no movement, and 0420 beside 420
stories.recipe: A written zero opening and closing is a position; leading zeros are kept (I1).

stories.title: A cell beyond the twelve columns
stories.recipe: A note printed in a thirteenth column.

stories.title: A GL account that cannot be read
stories.recipe: A GL line whose account is an Excel error could be any account's.

stories.title: A GL amount with a thousands separator and a wide GL line
stories.recipe: 12,950.00 has a thousands separator; a reviewer's mark sits in a sixth column.
